channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth cools as inflation risks build – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank economists Sanjay Raja and Maui Brennan say the UK enters autumn as the fastest-growing G7 economy, helped by strong ICT and AI-related investment and improving productivity.

item.title: Euro struggles as softer-than-expected US econoomic data offer little relief
item.description: EUR/USD struggles to attract buyers on Tuesday despite below-forecast US economic data, as the US Dollar (USD) shows little weakness following the release. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1601 after touching an intraday low of 1.1587, but remains down roughly 0.14% on the day.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed risks and election scenarios – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ macro team, led by Jayati Bharadwaj, Howard Du and Linda Cheng, maintains a bearish view on the Dollar despite a hawkish market reaction to Chair Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech.

item.title: Gold: Pricing stays supported as Fed path questioned – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that positioning in Gold remains resilient despite a more hawkish Jackson Hole speech from Fed Chair Warsh.

item.title: Gold sellers retain control despite US manufacturing PMI miss
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its pullback from the more-than-three-month high touched last week and falls to a fresh two-week low on Tuesday.

item.title: US ISM Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.6 in August
item.description: In August, the US manufacturing sector's economy lost some momentum. Indeed, the ISM Manufacturing PMI dropped from 55.6 in July to 54.6, which was also lower than analysts' predictions of 55.2.

item.title: Breaking: US JOLTS Job Openings rise to 7.27 million in July vs. 7.3 million expected
item.description: The number of job openings rose slightly to 7.271 million in July from 7.182 million in June, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Tuesday. This reading came in below the market expectation of 7.3 million.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Yield cap and intervention shape risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that rising global bond yields and firmer Oil prices have pushed 30-year US Treasury yields back to pre-buyback levels, while USD/JPY has largely retraced its post-intervention slump.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as Japan’s 10-year yield hits 3% for first time since 1996
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 160.05 on Tuesday at the time of writing, gaining 0.19% on the day, as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro area: Inflation jump supports ECB hike – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Vincent Stamer notes that Euro area headline inflation rose to 3.3% in August from 2.9% in July, driven mainly by higher energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Fed’s Barr keeps rate hike on the table as inflation persists
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said inflation remains too high and warned that a rate hike could become necessary if price pressures fail to moderate soon.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Pair extends recovery above key moving averages
item.description: USD/CHF ticks higher on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) recoups most of the previous day’s losses. Hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and rising US Treasury yields keep the Greenback underpinned near its recent highs.

item.title: “Good news” on inflation: ECB’s Nagel sees no second-round effects
item.description: Joachim Nagel, European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member and Bundesbank President, expressed confidence on Tuesday in the global economic outlook despite geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI seen hiking as inflation risks build – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Jester Koh expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to deliver two consecutive 25bps rate hikes starting from the December 2026 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, as headline inflation is projected to breach the upper end of the RBI’s 2–6% band by 3QFY27.

item.title: S&P 500: Strong earnings but stretched valuation risk – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategists highlight that the S&P 500 has hit a fresh record high in August, supported by an exceptionally strong Q2 earnings season with roughly 50% year-on-year EPS growth.

item.title: Australian Dollar retreats as rising US yields overshadow upbeat Chinese PMI
item.description: AUD/USD declines 0.29% on Tuesday, trading around 0.7145 at the time of writing. The Australian Dollar (AUD) struggles to retain the momentum initially generated by encouraging Chinese economic data, while the US Dollar (USD) benefits from rising US Treasury yields.

item.title: Canadian Dollar retreats as US Dollar benefits from Fed rate hike bets
item.description: USD/CAD trades on the front foot on Tuesday, supported by a firmer US Dollar (USD), while trade tensions between the United States (US) and Canada and diverging Federal Reserve (Fed) and Bank of Canada (BoC) policy expectations weigh on the Canadian Dollar (CAD).

item.title: US Dollar: Warsh boost fades as Fed pricing holds – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar has surrendered around half of its post-Jackson Hole gains, even as front-end US rates remain firmly supported. He argues that concerns over long-end yields and potential Treasury intervention are feeding a debasement narrative.

item.title: Euro: ECB tightening seen limiting downside – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD is trading heavy just below 1.1600 as Eurozone August Consumer Price Index (CPI) confirmed easing underlying inflation, with core and services measures slowing.

item.title: European Central Bank: Inflation risks support another hike - Nordea
item.description: Nordea strategists note that Euro-area flash inflation rose to 3.3% year-on-year in August, driven mainly by higher energy inflation, while core inflation edged down to 2.4% on weaker services.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Strong GDP underpins higher INR yields – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan highlights India’s strong GDP data, with Q1 FY2026-27 growth at 7.8% year-on-year versus 7.1% consensus. Resilient domestic demand, robust credit growth and supportive fiscal policy underpin his view that Indian rates are likely to grind higher.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD extends reversal below $4.400 amid Fed hawkish repricing
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) resumed its decline on Tuesday, following a flat performance on Monday, reaching fresh two-week lows at $4,375 so far, posting a nearly 7% decline from last week’s peak, near $4,700.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy pressure and FX path – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Jane Foley examines Japanese Yen (JPY) weakness amid Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s preference for low interest rates, US Treasury pressure on BoJ policy and recent coordinated FX intervention.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Upbeat US Dollar stresses on major currency pair
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades 0.2% lower to near 1.1593 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar: September hike odds stay elevated – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar has recovered most of its recent pullback as Fed funds futures price a 67% chance of a 25 bps rate hike on September 16 and 60 bps of tightening over twelve months.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains on India's upbeat Q2 GDP, narrowed fiscal deficit data
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains sharply against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The USD/INR pair slumps to near 94.80, the lowest level in two months, amid likely Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, stronger-than-expected Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data and a narrowed Fiscal Deficit.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade tensions and extended BoC hold – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities highlights asymmetric upside risk in USD/CAD as US–Canada trade tensions escalate.

item.title: Silver drops below $65 as hawkish Fed bets weigh on XAG/USD
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Tuesday, trading around $64.85 at the time of writing, down 2.54% on the day. The white metal slips below the key $65.50 area as prospects of tighter US monetary policy continue to weigh on precious metals.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slumps against US Dollar amid firm hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is down 0.35%, marginally below 0.5900 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro extends losses against British Pound as Eurozone inflation fails to impress
item.description: The Euro (EUR) heads south against the British Pound (GBP) on Tuesday, weighed by somewhat softer inflationary pressures on the Eurozone and downbeat German Retail Sales figures.
